full_text:
Season player prop bets have trickled out at various sportsbooks since free agency started the 2026 league year, and wagers for the top rookies were released since the NFL Draft concluded. I recently broke down the initial [2026 Rookie of the Year Odds](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-rookie-of-the-year-awards). It’s time to dive into these numbers to see if there’s any value in these initial lines. I [correctly identified](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2025/rookie-player-props#/) the over on __Quinshon Judkins__’ rushing yards prop in this article last year. Let’s find another winner in this year’s rookie class.

Wagering your hard-earned money in May and waiting for bets to be settled in eight months isn’t the easiest pill to swallow. Nevertheless, if we can get the best of the lines before the markets fully mature in the future, it will make the wait until the end of the season worth it in the long run. Shop around for the best lines and odds if you have access to multiple sportsbooks. You’ll see more volatility between books on NFL Futures in the off-season than you’ll see on game lines and player props during the season. Let’s see if we can find some value in these rookie player props.

\>Be sure to check out [Brolley’s Best Bets: 2026 NFL Futures](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2026/best-bets) for my favorite futures bets all offseason…Subscribe to the Best Bets Podcast on your [favorite platform](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/podcasts/show/nfl-best-bets) and on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@FantasyPointsBetting) for year-round NFL betting talk…Join our “#official-bets” [Fantasy Points Discord](https://www.fantasypoints.com/media/discord) to see our staff's wagers as soon as we make them!

{{CTA|DataSuite}}

Quarterback
-----------

#### __{{Fernando Mendoza|QB|LV|26740}}__, Las Vegas Raiders

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 2230 yards, 13.2 TDs

+   __DraftKings passing yards__: 2499.5 (-110/-110); 147.0 per game

+   __FanDuel passing yards__: 2500.5 (-114/-114); 147.1 per game
+   __Caesars passing yards__: 2500.5 (-115/-115); 147.1 per game
+   __Bet365 passing yards__: 2699.5 (-110/-110); 158.8 per game
+   __FanDuel passing TDs__: 12.5 (-122/-108); .74 per game
+   __Caesars passing TDs__: 13.5 (+100/-130); .74 per game
+   __Bet365 passing TDs__: 14.5 (+115/-145); .85 per game

This bet could go down to whether Mendoza or __Kirk Cousins__ is the starting quarterback to open the season. I’m fairly confident the Raiders will bring Mendoza along slowly this season, and our projections reflect that same sentiment, but it’s far from a guarantee that Cousins opens the season as the starter. Mendoza will be watching from the sidelines in September if minority owner __Tom Brady__ has as much power as it seems from the outside. Brady called it a “[tragedy](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zyclRMckosM)” to force rookie quarterbacks to play early in their careers. The Raiders will pay $11.3 million guaranteed to Cousins to mentor Mendoza this season, which is a starter’s salary and makes him the 20th-highest paid QB in average annual value. Our projections have Mendoza easily going under his yardage prop, but I’m going to stay away because I could see the Raiders succumbing to the pressure and playing Mendoza if Las Vegas gets out of the gates slowly with Cousins at quarterback.

Running Backs
-------------

#### __{{Jeremiyah Love|RB|ARI|26768}}__, Arizona Cardinals

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 1015.1 yards, 7.7 TDs

+   __DraftKings rushing yards__: 899.5 (-110/-110); 52.9 YPG
+   __FanDuel rushing yards__: 900.5 (-114/-114); 53.0 YPG
+   __Bet365 rushing yards__: 974.5 (-110/-110); 57.3 YPG
+   __Caesars rushing yards__: 925.5 (-115/-115); 54.4 YPG
+   __Caesars rushing TDs__: 5.5 (-115/-115); .32 per game

​​Arizona took plenty of heat for selecting a running back third overall, and Love has the highest total value of a contract at the position. He figures to see plenty of work immediately since the organization will want to justify the selection. Running backs selected inside the top 10 since 2015 have had a strong record of immediate success. __Ashton Jeanty__ (2025), __Bijan Robinson__ (2023), __Saquon Barkley__ (2018), __Leonard Fournette__ (2017), __Ezekiel Elliott__ (2016), and __Todd Gurley__ (2015) each reached 975+ rushing yards as rookies. That’s the number Love needs to reach to clear his rushing yards prop at the various sportsbooks. Jeanty (976 yards) and Bijan (975) each needed every carry they could get over 17 games to reach that threshold. I’m slightly worried the Cardinals don’t need to force-feed Love, especially if they fall out of contention and are looking to lose games late in the season to start their March for Arch (Manning). Arizona handed $8 million in guaranteed money to __Tyler Allgeier__ in free agency, and __James Conner__ and __Trey Benson__ remain in the mix for now. Love could go under his yardage prop if Allgeier steals enough carries away, as he did to Bijan when his prop was set at 1100.5 yards in 2023.

#### __{{Jadarian Price|RB|SEA|26765}}__, Seattle Seahawks

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 984.4 yards, 6.6 TDs

+   __Caesars__ __rushing yards__: 725.5 (-115/-115); 42.7 YPG
+   __Caesars rushing TDs__: 5.5 (-115/-115); .32 per game

Price went from being a potential backup as a Day 2 pick to landing one of the few starting jobs available when the Seahawks selected him with the final pick of the first round. __Kenneth Walker__ left for Kansas City in free agency, and __Zach Charbonnet__ may not be ready to play until mid-season after tearing his ACL in mid-January. The Packers didn’t tender restricted free agent __Emanuel Wilson__ this offseason, and he signed with the Seahawks, where he’ll be the primary player standing between Price and a majority of the carries in Seattle’s run-heavy attack to start the season. The Seahawks could still be hesitant to put too much on Price’s plate right out of the gates since he never logged more than 120 carries in any of his three seasons at Notre Dame. Price is the favorite to be the team’s lead back early in the season, but __Mike Macdonald__’s teams have rotated backs early in his tenure, and Charbonnet will be back to steal work by the middle of the season. Price is positioned to go over this lower total, but I’d be a little cautious with this seemingly perfect setup for a back that hasn’t handled a large workload since high school.

Wide Receivers
--------------

#### __{{Carnell Tate|WR|TEN|26752}}__, Tennessee Titans

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 724.9 yards, 4.8 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 774.5 (-110/-110); 45.6 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 775.5 (-114/-114); 45.6 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 749.5 (-110/-110); 44.1 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 800.5 (-115/-115); 47.1 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving TDs__: 4.5 (+120/-155); .26 per game

Tate received better draft capital than expected when the Titans selected Tate fourth overall to give last year’s first overall pick, __Cam Ward__, a big-time weapon to develop with. Brett Whitefield [ranked](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) Tate directly between __A.J. Brown__ and __CeeDee Lamb__ as a top-10 WR evaluation in his 11th year of scouting college prospects. He’s the latest first-round talent in the last five drafts from Ohio State, joining __Emeka Egbuka__ (2025), __Marvin Harrison__ (2024), __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ (2023), and __Garrett Wilson__ (2022). Tate will immediately compete to be the #1 WR, and it’s promising that the new staff prioritized getting Ward a weapon at the top of the draft. The staff also handed __Wan’Dale Robinson__ $38 million guaranteed, who soaked up 140 targets in each of his last two seasons under new OC __Brian Daboll__. __Calvin Ridley__ is still around, and he has the most experience with Ward among Tennessee’s top receivers. Tate previously dealt with heavy target competition from Harrison, Egbuka, and __Jeremiah Smith__, Ohio State’s next top-five pick in 2027. Tate topped out at 875 yards in 11 games last season, and I lean slightly to the under on his receiving yards prop based on his target competition.

#### __{{Jordyn Tyson|WR|NO|26751}}__, New Orleans Saints

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 748.2 yards, 4.2 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 774.5 (-110/-110); 45.6 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 800.5 (-114/-114); 47.1 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 799.5 (-110/-110); 47.0 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 800.5 (-115/-115); 47.1 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving TDs__: 4.5 (+100/-130); .26 per game

Tyson surged up boards late in the pre-draft process because of his ceiling potential, but he was a mid-to-late first-round pick for most of the process because of his significant injury history. He missed time in each of his four college seasons because of knee, collarbone, and hamstring injuries. The Saints were willing to take a small gamble on Tyson, and he landed in one of the NFL’s more friendly offenses. __Kellen Moore__ has consistently called one of the faster-paced offenses at his different stops, and the Saints ranked 10th in plays per game (63.2) last year. Tyson is the clear #2 option behind __Chris Olave__, but this passing attack could be highly consolidated between __Tyler Shough__’s top two WRs. I lean toward Tyson’s over in New Orleans’ emerging offense, but his durability concerns are enough to keep me away from this 50/50 proposition. I’d much rather wager on him in an Offensive Rookie of the Year market if he does stay healthy and hits his ceiling.

#### __{{Makai Lemon|WR|PHI|26748}}__, Philadelphia Eagles

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 695.4 yards, 4.2 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 649.5 (-110/-110); 38.2 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 650.5 (-114/-114); 38.3 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 649.5 (-110/-110); 38.2 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 600.5 (-115/-115); 35.3 YPG

The Eagles have made it abundantly clear that __A.J. Brown__ isn’t a part of their future plans after trading up three spots to select Lemon at No. 20. Philadelphia previously traded for __Dontayvion Wicks__ and signed __Hollywood Brown__ before the draft, which means Lemon has a path to the #2 WR role early in his career. Lemon will get opportunities on the perimeter, but most of his routes are likely to come from the slot as a rookie. He’ll have significant target competition from __Dallas Goedert__ and second-round pick __Eli Stowers__ in the middle of the field, which is an area of the field __Jalen Hurts__ has been reluctant to throw to during his career. Hurts ranked 35th out of 36 QBs [on the rate of throws over the middle of the field](https://x.com/ffdataroma/status/2047673161395716566?s=20) at 16.3%. The Eagles have ranked 24th (29.2) and 32nd (26.4) in pass attempts per game in their first two seasons with __Saquon Barkley__ on the roster. At least Hurts concentrated his attempts between Brown and Smith — more than 50% of the targets went to those two WRs in that span — but I think it’s a leap of faith to project Lemon to step into a large target share immediately.

#### __{{K.C. Concepcion|WR|CLE}}__, Cleveland Browns

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 550.1 yards, 3.3 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 624.5 (-110/-110); 36.7 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 650.5 (-114/-114); 38.3 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 649.5 (-110/-110); 38.2 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 675.5 (-115/-115); 39.7 YPG

Concepcion needs to beat out the underwhelming __Jerry Jeudy__ to become Cleveland’s #1 WR right away, and he’ll eventually compete with __Harold Fannin__ to be the #1 option in Cleveland’s passing game. Brett Whitefield saw shades of __Brandon Aiyuk__ in Concepcion because of his dynamic ability after the catch, which __Todd Monken__ should take advantage of immediately. Monken will put him in motion and use him to stretch the field, and he’ll get him the ball in space to take advantage of his ability with the ball in his hands as he did with __Zay Flowers__ the last three seasons. My biggest concern for Concepcion is the quarterback play he’ll receive from __Deshaun Watson__ and __Shedeur Sanders__ next season. I’m going to pass on wagering on Concepcion’s prop since I already wagered on him to win the [Offensive Rookie of the Year](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-rookie-of-the-year-awards#/) at +3000 odds in case he quickly becomes the focal point of this passing attack.

#### __{{Omar Cooper|WR|NYJ|26760}}__, New York Jets

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 707.0 yards, 4.3 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 549.5 (-110/-110); 32.3 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 575.5 (-114/-114); 33.9 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 574.5 (-110/-110); 33.8 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 575.5 (-115/-115); 33.9 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving TDs__: 3.5 (+110/-140); .21 per game

The Jets took the best-player-available approach when they selected __Kenyon Sadiq__ at No. 16 instead of __Makai Lemon__, but they still got a WR when they traded up to take Cooper at No. 30. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) Cooper as a run-after-catch demon who is reminiscent of __D.J. Moore__, but he does overlap as a middle-of-the-field receiver with Sadiq. __Garrett Wilson__ is still the clear top option in this passing attack after he finished behind only __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ in target share (30.4%) and first-read share (43.9%). Cooper’s first-round draft capital gives him a path to the #2 WR spot, but he’ll have to earn it over __Adonai Mitchell__, who flashed after he was traded to the Jets despite a league-worst quarterback situation. __Geno Smith__ is positioned to bounce back after posting an 84.7 passer rating and a league-high 17 INTs, but I’m skeptical he can support all of New York’s receiving options at this stage of his career. I lean toward Cooper disappointing a bit and falling short of his props in a passing game that has more talented options.

Tight End
---------

#### __{{Kenyon Sadiq|TE|NYJ|26755}}__, New York Jets

\>__Fantasy Points Projection__: 647.4 yards, 4.2 TDs

+   __Draftkings receiving yards__: 474.5 (-110/-110); 27.9 YPG
+   __FanDuel receiving yards__: 450.5 (-114/-114); 26.5 YPG
+   __Bet365 receiving yards__: 499.5 (-110/-110); 29.4 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving yards__: 450.5 (-115/-115); 26.5 YPG
+   __Caesars receiving TDs__: 3.5 (+115/-145); .21 per game

I didn’t love Sadiq’s landing spot in a Jets offense that already has 2025 second-round pick __Mason Taylor__ at TE. The Jets added __Omar Cooper__ to their receiving corps later in the first round, but recent history tells us Sadiq will play a prominent role early in his career based on his top half of the first-round draft capital. __Colston Loveland__ (713 yards), __Tyler Warren__ (817), __Brock Bowers__ (1194), and __Kyle Pitts__ (1026) each easily cruised over 500 receiving yards and topped their season-long yardage props as top-16 draft picks since 2021. __T.J. Hockenson__ was the last rookie TE selected inside the top-16 picks who failed to reach 500+ yards after the Lions picked him eighth overall in 2019. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/te) Sadiq as a mutant — he posted a perfect [SPORQ score](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/stats/sporq/te#/) at the combine — who has the necessary receiving chops to be one of the NFL’s top TEs. The Jets didn’t draft Sadiq in the middle of the first round to waste him on the bench as a rookie. He should get every opportunity to be a target-earner, and he can turn any pass into a long gain with his 4.39 speed.
